title: Three-Word Definition · Pair relay
hook: Find a game, gather your friends and start playing.

knows: The group wants an activity to play together.
doesNotKnow: The setup, turn and ending for this house-rule format.

misconception: The group has to know a complicated rulebook before starting.
objective: Learn how to play Three-Word Definition · Pair relay with friends.

claims.text: Original house rules: Write familiar objects on slips. The lead picks a slip and gives exactly three spoken words as a clue, excluding the object's name. The group guesses the object. Form pairs. On each pair’s turn, both people make separate attempts with fresh challenges, helping only their partner. The pair earns one point only if both succeed. Each pair has two turns. Highest score wins.
claims.source: Original playable house-rule proposal; not an authoritative ruleset for a traditional game.

claims.text: For this version: 4, 6 or 8 players; materials: Paper and pencil.
claims.source: Proposed setup and player range for this activity.

recall.question: In Three-Word Definition, what counts as a successful turn?
options: The lead skips the turn without attempting it.
The group ends the round before anyone plays.
